cap_enforcement_note: CAP ENFORCEMENT FOR THIS ITEM IS INTACT, AND IT IS THE ITEM'S OWN DOING, NOT THE RUNNER'S. Recorded explicitly so nobody later reads a clean A2-B2R cap history as evidence of runner-level cap safety in general. (1) THE RUNNER DOES NOT ENFORCE CAPS. queue_runner.cap_watch is a runaway guard that REPORTS: it writes CAP_OVERRUN.txt beside the run at 1.00 x cap_core_min_registered (or ESTIMATE_OVERRUN.txt at 1.10 x the estimate where no cap is registered) and NEVER TERMINATES (scripts/queue_runner.py:664-679). The script's own module docstring at :14-21 concedes this: it states that the non-enforcement is a property of the runner AS BUILT, NOT a permission any charter grants, and that COMPUTE_BUDGET_CHARTER.md:197 says the OPPOSITE -- 'A budget overrun stops the run. It does not get a new budget.' -- as does CLAUDE.md rule 12. Runner-side enforcement is pre-registered at docs/standards/RUNNER_CAP_ENFORCEMENT_CLAUSE.md (D539) and is ADVISORY, INERT and OFF; switching it on is Sanaa's decision alone. (2) FOR THIS ITEM THE CAP IS ENFORCED ANYWAY, by the item's own frozen launcher: run_a2b2r.sh:110 runs the solve under `timeout ${CAP_WALL_S}s` with CAP_WALL_S=600 (:56) at RANKS=4 (:57), i.e. 600 s wall x 4 ranks / 60 = the registered 40.0 core-min cap (prereg:446). timeout(1) kills the process group; the cap therefore STOPS this run rather than merely flagging it. (3) THE COROLLARY. Because enforcement is WALL-CLOCK and not a core-minute meter, contention is charged to the item: the registered point is 266.5 wall s at 4 ranks, so the cap tolerates a 2.25x slowdown and no more. Beyond that the item is CAP-STOPPED and, under CLAUDE.md rule 12, does not get a new budget. That is why box weather governed the hold and why the release is gated on the runner's own core_fraction arithmetic (see release_record).

release_record.why_the_hold_was_wrong: The hold was placed on box weather, on the assumption that the runner is not load-aware and would launch into contention. It IS load-aware, and it implements the hold's own release condition better than the hold did. Three gates sit immediately above the runner's ONLY launch site (scripts/queue_runner.py:946-957), fed by a /proc/stat busy delta and NOT by loadavg: (i) busy >= busy_ceiling (85%) returns HELD for the whole tick; (ii) busy_cores + ranks > core_fraction x ncpu -- with ranks=4, core_fraction=0.9 and ncpu=16 this requires busy_cores <= 10.4 of 16, i.e. the box at or below about 65% busy, which IS the hold's 'at least 4 genuinely idle cores' condition; (iii) MemAvailable < the entry's memory_floor_gb (12.0 GB here). Gates (ii) and (iii) are first-fit `continue`, so the entry simply waits for a tick where the box has room and is re-tested every 60 s.
release_record.why_held_was_worse_than_the_drop_path: AN ENTRY IN held/ IS INVISIBLE TO THE DAEMON. queue_runner.list_entries globs `(root/team).glob('*.json')` NON-RECURSIVELY (scripts/queue_runner.py:434-442), so held/ is never read and the entry would have waited for ever. A hand-rolled hold traded a runner that enforces the condition on every tick for a directory the runner cannot see.
